classification.difficultyReason: Compute the horizontal glide distance with tan, then convert units and subtract the 16 km to the runway. This is the p10-q15 task plus one interpretation step. No diagram is supplied.

content.prompt:
A plane descends towards an airport along a straight path at an angle of depression of $3^\circ$. When the plane is at a height of $950\text{ m}$, the start of the runway is $16\text{ km}$ away horizontally.
How far beyond the start of the runway will the plane touch down? Give your answer to the nearest $0.1\text{ km}$.

answer.worked:
Let $x$ be the horizontal distance to the touchdown point in kilometres. The angle of elevation from the touchdown point equals the angle of depression, and $950\text{ m}=0.95\text{ km}$.
$$\begin{align*}\tan 3^\circ&=\frac{0.95}{x}\\x&=\frac{0.95}{\tan 3^\circ}\\&\approx18.127\text{ km}\\\text{Distance beyond runway start}&=18.127-16\\&\approx2.1\text{ km}\end{align*}$$
